elements.quote: This systematic review aimed to identify and characterise models for malaria control optimization for resource allocation in limited resource settings and assess their strengths and limitations.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: This systematic review aimed to identify and characterise models for malaria control optimization for resource allocation in limited resource settings and assess their strengths and limitations.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective of the review explicitly.

elements.quote: Editorials, commentaries, opinion papers, conference abstracts, media reports, letters, bulletins, pre-prints, grey literature, non-English language studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses were excluded from the search.
elements.reason: The abstract reports exclusion criteria but does not specify the main inclusion criteria beyond '15 met the inclusion criteria'.

elements.quote: a comprehensive search across PubMed and Embase databases was performed of peer-reviewed literature published from inception until June 2024.
elements.reason: The abstract names the information sources (PubMed, Embase) and the end date of the search (June 2024).
The abstract does not mention any risk of bias or quality assessment methods; the ISPOR assessment is only described in the Methods (text_8).
The abstract does not describe methods used to present or synthesize results (e.g., narrative synthesis); synthesis methods appear only in the main text (text_10).

elements.quote: The search yielded 2950 records, of which 15 met the inclusion criteria. The studies were carried out mainly in countries in Africa (53.3%)... The most used interventions for analyses were insecticide-treated bed nets (93.3%), IRS (80.0%)...
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies (15) and summarizes study characteristics, but does not report the number of participants.

elements.quote: The methods used for estimating health benefits were compartmental models (40.0%), individual-based models (40.0%), static models (13.0%) and linear regression model (7%).
elements.reason: The abstract reports descriptive results (model types, data use, administrative levels) but does not present results for main outcomes with numbers of studies/participants per outcome in an outcome-specific manner.

elements.quote: A narrative synthesis of the study characteristics was performed.
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted; a narrative synthesis was performed, so no summary estimate applies.

elements.quote: This review identified available optimization models for malaria resource allocation.
elements.reason: The review does not compare groups with effect estimates; no direction-of-effect statement is applicable.
The abstract's conclusion does not summarize limitations of the included evidence such as risk of bias, inconsistency, or imprecision.

elements.quote: The findings highlighted the need for country-specific analysis for malaria control optimization, the use of country-specific epidemiological and cost data in performing modelling analyses... It is critical that the future modelling efforts account for fairness and target at risk malaria populations that are hard-to-reach to maximize impact.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the findings and their implications for future modelling efforts.
No funding source is stated in the abstract.

elements.quote: Trial registration : PROSPERO Registration number: CRD42023436966
elements.reason: The abstract section includes the register name (PROSPERO) and registration number (CRD42023436966).

elements.quote: Despite advances made in curbing the global malaria burden since the 2000s, progress has stalled, in part due to a plateauing of the financing available to implement needed interventions. In 2020, approximately 3.3 billion USD was invested globally for malaria interventions, falling short of the targeted 6.8 billion USD set by the GTS, increasing the financial gap between desirable and actual investment.
elements.reason: The abstract background describes the current state of knowledge (stalled progress, financing gap) and the uncertainty the review addresses.

elements.quote: Models for malaria control optimization are used to disentangle the most efficient interventions or packages of interventions for inherently constrained budgets. This systematic review aimed to identify and characterise models for malaria control optimization for resource allocation in limited resource settings and assess their strengths and limitations.
elements.reason: The importance and need for the review are explained: constrained budgets require optimization models, and the review aims to identify and characterise them.
No evidence in the retrieved text indicates that similar prior systematic reviews exist; the manuscript does not cite or discuss a previous review being updated or replicated.
This is a review of optimization modelling studies rather than a review of intervention effects; no proposed mechanism of action of an intervention is required or reported.
No logic model is presented or discussed in the retrieved evidence; the review characterises existing models rather than evaluating a complex intervention itself.

elements.quote: The research question for this review was ' Are there English-language publications in peer-reviewed scientific journals describing how models have been used to allocate resources for malaria interventions in limited resource settings?' The main aim of this review was to identify and characterize models for malaria control optimization for resource allocation in malaria control and elimination settings and to identify their strengths and limitations.
elements.reason: The review explicitly states both a research question and the main aim/objective, also echoed in the abstract ('This systematic review aimed to identify and characterise models for malaria control optimization...').

elements.quote: The main aim of this review was to identify and characterize models for malaria control optimization for resource allocation in malaria control and elimination settings and to identify their strengths and limitations.
elements.reason: This is a review of optimization models for resource allocation, not a review of intervention effects comparing interventions; no PICO-formatted planned comparisons are reported and the framework does not apply.

elements.quote: Studies containing an optimization model (mathematical or statistical); (6) All studies with human Plasmodium species; (7) Studies with two or more interventions; (8) Cost data were used in combination with the model outputs; (9) Outcomes/health benefits were clearly stated and/or measured.
elements.reason: Inclusion criteria specify eligible study designs (optimization models), population (human Plasmodium, any subgroup), setting (any geographical region), interventions (two or more), and outcome requirements. No follow-up requirement applies to modelling studies.

elements.quote: (1) Were scientific peer-reviewed journals written in English; (2) Were published before 30th June 2024;
elements.reason: Report characteristics are specified: publication status (peer-reviewed), language (English), and dissemination date (before 30 June 2024). Exclusion criteria in text_9 confirm exclusions of non-English and non-peer-reviewed report types.

elements.quote: The following records were excluded: (1) Editorials, commentaries, opinion papers, conference abstracts, media reports, letters, bulletins, pre-prints, grey literature; (2) Non-English language studies; (3) Systematic reviews, meta-analyses.
elements.reason: The review does not distinguish exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported; exclusion reasons listed relate to publication type, language, and study type only.

elements.quote: A narrative synthesis of the study characteristics was performed.
elements.reason: A narrative synthesis of study characteristics is reported, but no explicit groups used in each synthesis are specified or linked to comparisons defined in the review objectives.

elements.quote: Each record in the search were included if they met all of the following criteria:
elements.reason: Notable restrictions (e.g., English-only, two or more interventions, cost data requirement) are stated without any rationale or justification for these restrictions.

elements.quote: A systematic search of peer-reviewed literature published from inception until June 2024 was conducted.
elements.reason: A date restriction (until June 2024) is reported, but no explicit date on which each database was last searched is given.

elements.quote: The databases PubMed and Embase (OVID) were searched for relevant studies using the following keywords...

No evidence that any study register, regulatory database, or online repository was searched to identify studies; PROSPERO was used only for protocol registration.
No websites, search engines, or other online sources were reported as searched.
No organisations or manufacturers were reported as contacted to identify studies; author email queries related to data extraction, not study identification.
No individuals were reported as contacted to identify studies.

elements.quote: In total, 14 articles from the database search and 1 article from bibliography were included in the final analysis (Fig. 1).
elements.reason: Reference lists (bibliography) were consulted, but the types of reference lists examined are not specified.
No backward or forward citation searching with seed reports, citation index, or search date is reported.
No journals or conference proceedings were directly consulted as sources; conference abstracts were explicitly excluded.

elements.quote: The databases PubMed and Embase (OVID) were searched for relevant studies using the following keywords: optimization model; malaria; control interventions; elimination interventions; and MeSH terms: resource allocation, models, linear programming, malaria, Plasmodium, communicable disease control, disease eradication. A detailed list of all search terms and results are available in Additional file 2.
elements.reason: Full search strategies for both databases are reported, including keywords, MeSH terms, Boolean combination, and a complete search string table (table_0) with blocks and AND/OR structure.

elements.quote: (1) Were scientific peer-reviewed journals written in English; (2) Were published before 30th June 2024;

No mention of natural-language processing or text-analysis tools for search term identification.

elements.quote: Each record was screened by two independent reviewers using the Rayyan software. The screening process involved a review of the titles and abstracts of each record... elements.reason: Two reviewers screened records at both the title/abstract stage and the full-text stage.

elements.quote: Each record was screened by two independent reviewers using the Rayyan software.
